title: Bekhorot 18
description: Can two things in human hands coincide exactly? The heifer brought by two equidistant towns settles the Rabbis’ view; then the twin firstborn lambs: Rabbi Tarfon’s “better one”, Rabbi Akiva’s “they assess”, the priestly gifts, the twin that died, Rabbi Ḥiyya’s two parables, and a new mishna about two ewes giving birth together.
topics: 📏 Can two matters in human hands coincide precisely? The towns equidistant from a slain man
🐑 Rabbi Tarfon: the healthier twin came out first; Rabbi Akiva: the priest takes the leaner
🌴 “While you were eating dates in Babylonia”: Rabbi Yoḥanan reads “they assess” from the latter clause
🍖 The priestly gifts from the second lamb: “two sides” for Rabbi Meir, “one who did not acquire” for Rabbi Yosei
⚖️ Rabbi Elazar and Rav Pappa: when everyone concedes
🔄 Rabbi Tarfon retracted: dividing the surviving twin
🧑‍🌾 Rabbi Ḥiyya’s parables of the shepherd and the homeowner, and the courtyard shared with the priest
🐏 New mishna: two ewes, two males and a female, and why each case had to be taught

a1.he: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאָמַר: אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן בִּידֵי אָדָם.

a2.he: נֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי: נִמְצָא מְכוָּּון בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת — לֹא הָיוּ עוֹרְפִין, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת שְׁתֵּי עֲגָלוֹת. מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם?

a3.he: וְתִיסְבְּרַאּ? אִי קָסָבַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, אַמַּאי לֹא הָיוּ עוֹרְפִים? יָבִיאוּ עֶגְלָה אַחַת בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת וְיַתְנוּ!

a4.he: אֶלָּא, לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, וְהָכָא בִּ״קְרוֹבָה״ וְלֹא קְרוֹבוֹת קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: ״קְרוֹבָה״ וְלֹא קְרוֹבוֹת, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: ״קְרוֹבָה״ וַאֲפִילּוּ קְרוֹבוֹת.

a5.he: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: תָּנָא נִמְצָא מְכוָּּון בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת שְׁתֵּי עֲגָלוֹת, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יָבִיאוּ עֶגְלָה אַחַת בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת וְיַתְנוּ.

a6.he: מַאי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן? אִי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, וּקְרוֹבָה — וַאֲפִילּוּ קְרוֹבוֹת, לַיְיתֵי תַּרְתֵּי! וְאִי ״קְרוֹבָה״ וְלֹא קְרוֹבוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ חֲדָא לָא לַיְיתֵי! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a7.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן? קָא סָבַר: הָהוּא דְּבָרִיא נָפֵק בְּרֵישָׁא.

a8.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: ״מְשַׁמְּנִין״ כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּהֵן נוֹטֵל כְּחוּשָׁה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהָא אֲנַן ״מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶן״ תְּנַן! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד דַּאֲכַלְתְּ כַּפְנְיָיתָא בְּבָבֶל, תַּרְגֵּימְנָא מִסֵּיפָא.

a9.he: דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה. וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ ״מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶן״ דְּכִי הֲדָדֵי פְּלִיגִי, הָכִי נָמֵי (לִיפַּלְגִי) [לִיפְלוֹג] גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי! אֶלָּא מַאי ״מְשַׁמְּנִין״ — שׁוֹמֶן יְהֵא בֵּינֵיהֶן, דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן: אַיְיתִי רְאָיָה דִּבְכוֹר הוּא וּשְׁקֹיל.

a10.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְחַיָּיב בְּמַתָּנוֹת, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הוֹאִיל וְכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בְּכוֹר הוּא — כּוּלֵּיהּ דִּידִי הוּא, אִי לָא בְּכוֹר הוּא — הַב לִי מַתָּנוֹת מִינֵּיהּ.

a11.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רָבָא: עָשׂוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְטָא לִידֵיהּ כְּמַאן דִּמְטָא לִידֵיהּ, וְזַבְּנֵיהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמוּמֵיהּ.

a12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּסְפֵק בְּכוֹר, שֶׁאֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן, שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּמַתָּנוֹת.

a13.he: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים מַאן? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי? פְּשִׁיטָא! עַד כָּאן לָא קָא פָטַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם, אֶלָּא דַּחֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן, דְּעָשׂוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה, אֲבָל אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — לָא!

a14.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דְּקָסָבַר דְּאִי מְחַיְּיבַתְּ לֵיהּ בְּמַתָּנוֹת — אָתֵי לֵיהּ לִידֵי גִּיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a15.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָתָנֵי סֵיפָא, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:

b1.he: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב. חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — אִין, אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — לָא!

b2.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ — לְדִידִי, אֲפִילּוּ אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן, דְּאִי מְחַיְּיבַתְּ לֵיהּ בְּמַתָּנוֹת אָתֵי לֵיהּ לִידֵי גִּיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה; לְדִידָךְ, אוֹדִי לִי מִיהָא הֵיכָא דַּחֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן, דְּעָשׂוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה; וְאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר: לָא.

b3.he: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּסְפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁפָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת. ״הַכֹּל מוֹדִים״ — מַאן? רַבִּי מֵאִיר? פְּשִׁיטָא! עַד כָּאן לָא קָמְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם אֶלָּא בִּסְפֵק בְּכוֹר, הוֹאִיל וּבָא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, אֲבָל סָפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר — לָא.

b4.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרַת מַתָּנוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ סְפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי? קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b5.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב!

b6.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲפִילּוּ סְפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר מְחַיַּיב, וְהָא דְּמִיפַּלְגִי בַּחֲלִיפִין — לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דְּפָטַר אֲפִילּוּ הֵיכָא דְּכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b7.he: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ. אַמַּאי יַחְלוֹקוּ? נִיחְזֵי: אִי שָׁמֵן מִית — דְּכֹהֵן הוּא, וְהַאי דְּאִיכָּא דְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת; וְאִי כָּחוּשׁ מִית — דְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת מִית, וְהַאי דְּאִיכָּא דְּכֹהֵן הוּא! אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: חָזַר בּוֹ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן.

b8.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה. אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה? לִשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה, שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ רוֹעֶה בֵּינֵיהֶם וּמִסְתַּלֵּק.

b9.he: וּמָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה? לְאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה.

b10.he: אֶלָּא בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא פְּלִיג בִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה, שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ רוֹעֶה וּמִסְתַּלֵּק? וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן פְּלִיג בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת? אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה — שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ רוֹעֶה בֵּינֵיהֶם וּמִסְתַּלֵּק, וּבְאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת — שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה.

b11.he: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בַּחֲצַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וְרוֹעֶה כֹּהֵן. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן סָבַר: אַקְנוֹיֵי קָא מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ בַּחֲצֵירוֹ, וְנִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִיתְעֲבִיד מִצְוָה בְּמָמוֹנֵיהּ, וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה, שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ רוֹעֶה בֵּינֵיהֶן וּמִסְתַּלֵּק.

b12.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא — לָא מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ מִידַּעַם, וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה.

b13.he: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי רְחֵילָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — שְׁנֵיהֶם לַכֹּהֵן. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — הַזָּכָר לַכֹּהֵן. שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה — אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֵן בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶן, וְהַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב.

b14.he: וְחַיָּיב בַּמַּתָּנוֹת, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר. מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה. שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b15.he: אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה, וְאַחַת לֹא בִּיכְּרָה, וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים, אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֵן בּוֹרֵר אֶת הַיָּפֶה. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶן, וְהַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב.

b16.he: וְחַיָּיב בַּמַּתָּנוֹת. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר, שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת. וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב. מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b17.he: גְּמָ׳ צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן קַמַּיְיתָא, בְּהַהִיא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דִּתְרֵי מֵחֲדָא.

b18.he: אֲבָל רְחֵילָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ, דִּתְרֵי מֵחֲדָא וְחַד מֵחֲדָא — אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, דְּהָךְ דִּילִידָא חַד שְׁבִיחַ טְפֵי.

b19.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הָא — בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ לֹא בִּיכְּרוּ, אֲבָל אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,

messages.text: Continued from 17b: the Gemara is asking whether, in the Rabbis’ view, two matters in human hands can coincide precisely. It tried to prove it from Rabbi Eliezer, who rules that two towns found equidistant from a slain man bring two heifers, and answered: No, Rabbi Eliezer…
Gemara

…holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says: It is possible for two matters that are in the hands of Heaven to coincide precisely, and all the more so matters that are in human hands. Consequently, one cannot cite Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion in order to determine the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.he: וקא מיבעיא לן לרבנן:
notes.en: He holds like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: and our question is about the Rabbis.

notes.he: ואכתי לרבא לא ידעינן דתנא קמא סבר אי אפשר לצמצם והויין שתיהן רחוקות כדאמרן בתנור:
notes.en: He holds like Rabbi Yosei [HaGelili]. And still, according to Rava [so the printed text; the sense seems to be: according to the Rabbis], we do not know whether the first tanna holds that it is impossible to coincide precisely, so that both [towns] count as distant, as we said about the oven [17b].

messages.text: Let us say that this is subject to a dispute between tanna’im, as it is taught in a baraita:
If the corpse of a slain person was found precisely between two towns, they would not break the heifer’s neck at all.
The two towns bring two heifers between them.

What, is it not correct to say that they disagree with regard to this matter, in that the first tanna holds that it is impossible for two matters to coincide precisely and Rabbi Eliezer holds that it is possible for two matters to coincide precisely?

notes.he: הילכך לא היו עורפין דכל אחת אומרת אני איני קרובה:
notes.en: It is impossible to coincide precisely: therefore they would not break the neck, since each town says: I am not the nearest.

notes.he: וקרובה אפילו קרובות:
notes.en: It is possible to coincide precisely: and “nearest” includes even [several] nearest towns.

messages.text: And how can you understand that to be the dispute? If the first tanna holds that it is impossible for two matters to coincide precisely, why does he claim that they would not break the heifer’s neck? Let them bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate that it is brought for the town that is actually nearest.
messages.quote: they would not break the heifer’s neck

notes.he: כדפרשינן לעיל:
notes.en: And stipulate: as we explained above.

notes.he: לתנא קמא אי אי אפשר לצמצם אם כן לא סגיא דלא הווייא חדא קרובה:
notes.en: And how can you understand: for the first tanna, if it is impossible to coincide precisely, then one of them must be the nearest.

notes.he: אם אני הקרובה תבא העגלה עלי ואם חברתי הקרובה תבא עליה:
notes.en: Let them bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate: If I am the nearest, let the heifer be on my account; and if my fellow [town] is the nearest, let it be on its account.

messages.text: Rather, with regard to these tanna’im, everyone agrees that it is possible for two matters to coincide precisely. And here they disagree over whether the singular form kerova in the phrase “the town which is nearest [kerova]” indicates that only the nearest town brings a heifer, and not the many nearest [kerovot] towns;

verse.he: וְהָיָה הָעִיר הַקְּרֹבָה אֶל־הֶחָלָל וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא עֶגְלַת בָּקָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא־עֻבַּד בָּהּ אֲשֶׁר לֹא־מָשְׁכָה בְּעֹל׃
verse.en: The elders of the town nearest to the corpse shall then take a heifer that has never been worked, which has never pulled in a yoke;

notes.he: דכרבי יוסי הגלילי סבירא להו:
notes.en: Everyone agrees it is possible to coincide precisely: they hold like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

messages.text: as the first tanna holds that it is derived from the term “kerova” that only the nearest town brings a heifer, and not multiple kerovot; and Rabbi Eliezer holds that although the verse states “kerova,” nevertheless this includes even multiple towns that are kerovot.
What conclusion was reached about the Rabbis’ opinion with regard to whether matters in human hands can coincide precisely?

notes.he: אליבא דרבנן:
notes.en: What conclusion was reached about it: according to the Rabbis.

notes.he: לרבנן אפשר או אי אפשר:
notes.en: What conclusion was reached about it: according to the Rabbis, is it possible or impossible?

messages.text: The Sages taught in a baraita:
If the slain person was found precisely between two towns,
The two towns bring two heifers between them;

notes.he: דאפשר לצמצם וקרובה אפי' קרובות:
notes.en: Two heifers: since it is possible to coincide precisely, and “nearest” includes even [several] nearest towns.

messages.text: They bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate that it is brought for the town that is nearest.

What do the Rabbis hold in this regard? If the Rabbis hold that is possible for two matters that are in human hands to coincide precisely, and the singular “kerova” includes even multiple towns, kerovot, then they should bring two heifers. And if they hold that “kerova” indicates: But not kerovot, then they should not bring even one heifer.
messages.quote: They bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate

notes.he: דהא לא מצי לאתנויי דהא שתיהן שוות:
notes.en: Let them bring two: since they cannot make a stipulation, as the two [towns] are equal.

messages.text: Rather, must one not conclude from it that the Rabbis hold: It is impossible for two matters to coincide precisely, and this is true even with regard to matters that are in human hands? Indeed, conclude from it that this is so.

notes.he: הילכך מצו לאתנויי:
notes.en: It is impossible to coincide precisely: therefore they can make a stipulation.

notes.he: אלא ש"מ אי אפשר לצמצם קסבר ומשום הכי יביאו אחת ויתנו כדאמרן:
notes.en: Rather, conclude from it that [the Rabbis] hold it is impossible to coincide precisely, and that is why they bring one and stipulate, as we said.

messages.text: The priest chooses the better of the two.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that in the case of a ewe that gave birth for the first time to two male offspring whose heads emerged as one,

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Tarfon? He holds that it is presumed that the healthier and better of the two emerged first, and therefore it belongs to the priest.
messages.quote: The priest chooses the better of the two

notes.he: דמרוב בריאותו קדם את אחיו:
notes.en: The healthy one came out first: out of its great vigor it went ahead of its brother.

messages.text: They assess the value of the lambs between them.
According to Rabbi Akiva, the priest takes the leaner of the two.

notes.he: לרבי עקיבא:
notes.en: The priest takes the lean one: according to Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: אמר ר' חייא משמיה דר' יוחנן משמנין דאמר ר' עקיבא היינו שישמו איזה הוא הכחוש מן האחד ויטול הכהן הכחוש בלבד:
notes.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba] said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: The “they assess” that Rabbi Akiva said means that they assess which of the two is the lean one, and the priest takes only the lean one.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan But didn’t we learn that they assess the value of the offspring between them, which indicates that the priest and owner divide their value?

notes.he: דמשמע מה שיפה השור מחבירו ואותן דמים יחלוקו:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn “they assess [meshammenin]”: which implies that whatever the one is worth more than the other, they divide that money.

notes.he: בשעה שלמד זה הלכה ממנו:
notes.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya [bar Abba] said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: at the time he learned this halakha from him.

notes.he: דמשמע שיחלקו העלוי בשוה:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn “they assess”: which implies that they divide the added value equally.

messages.text: @Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba While you were eating dates in Babylonia, we in Eretz Yisrael explained it based on the latter clause in the mishna.

notes.he: בעוד שהייתה אוכל תמרים בבבל ומעדן עצמך:
notes.en: While you were eating dates [kafnayata] in Babylonia: while you were eating dates in Babylonia and pampering yourself.

notes.he: להאי מילתא דר' עקיבא ודייקנא לה מסיפא:
notes.en: We explained it: this statement of Rabbi Akiva, and we inferred it from the latter clause.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס בעוד שהייתה אוכל תמרים בבבל ומעדן את עצמך טרחנו ליישבה וכן פירש רבינו שמואל בפ' בית כור (ב"ב דף קז:) וקשה דהוה ליה למנקט תמרים דכפנייתא הוא לשון גריעותא כדאמר בריש בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כח:) דכפניות אין ניקחות בכסף מעשר אלא אומר דה"פ מוטב שיהיה לך להיות אצלי ולטרוח בהלכה ולפרשה משהייתה אוכל כפניות בבבל:
notes.en: While you were eating kafnayata in Babylonia, we explained it: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: while you were eating dates in Babylonia and pampering yourself, we toiled to settle it; and Rabbeinu Shmuel explained it the same way in chapter Beit Kor (Bava Batra 107b). But this is difficult: he should have said “dates” [temarim], for kafnayata is a term of inferiority, as is said at the beginning of Bekhol Me’arvin (Eruvin 28b) that kafniyot may not be bought with second-tithe money. Rather, I say the meaning is: it would have been better for you to be with me, toiling in halakha and explaining it, than to be eating kafniyot in Babylonia.

notes.he: תמרים רעים:
notes.en: Kafnayata: poor dates.

messages.text: As the latter clause teaches: If one of the two born together died, Rabbi Tarfon says: The priest and the owner divide the remaining lamb, and Rabbi Akiva says: Since there is uncertainty to whom it belongs, it remains in the possession of the owner, as the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

notes.he: מדוקיא דסיפא המוציא מחבירו ע"ה דאי ס"ד משמנין ביניהן לחלוק הכל בשוה בסיפא נמי ליפלגו בשוה:
notes.en: From the latter clause: from the inference of the latter clause, “the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.” For if it should enter your mind that “they assess between them” means dividing everything equally, then in the latter clause too let them divide equally.

messages.text: And if it enters your mind that when Rabbi Akiva said that they assess the value between them he meant that they divide the value between them, then in the latter clause too, let them divide the value of the remaining offspring between them instead of leaving it with the owner.

notes.he: דלתרוייהו יהא חלק בשניהם ה"נ יחלוקו את החי:
notes.en: That they divide between them: that both have a share in both [lambs]; then here too let them divide the living one.

messages.text: Rather, what does: They assess [meshammenin] the value between them, mean? It means that the additional fat [shumman] of the better twin will be the subject of dispute between them, as the owner says to the priest: Bring a proof that the better one is the firstborn, and take it.

notes.he: מה שאחד שמן יפה מחבירו יהא מוטל ביניהם ועליו יבאו לדין ויטעון ישראל לכהן אייתי ראיה כו' כי היכי דסבר ר' עקיבא בסיפא המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: The fat will be between them: whatever the one is fatter and better than the other is left lying between them, and over it they come to judgment, and the Israelite claims against the priest: Bring a proof, etc., just as Rabbi Akiva holds in the latter clause: the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

notes.he: שמן יהא ביניהן. כלומר דסבירא ליה לר' עקיבא דיד כהן על התחתונה דשמין כחוש והשומן שחברו מוטב מזה הוא ביניהן ואמר לו ישראל אייתי ראיה דהאי בכור ושקול ואי לא לית לך תו מידי:
notes.en: Rather, what does “they assess” mean? The fat will be between them. That is, Rabbi Akiva holds that the priest has the lower hand: they assess the lean one, and the fat by which the other is better than this one is [left] between them. The Israelite says to him: Bring a proof that this one is the firstborn, and take it; and if not, you have nothing more.

messages.text: And the second lamb that remains in the possession of the owner must graze until it becomes blemished, at which point he may slaughter and eat it,
and he is obligated to have the gifts of the priesthood, i.e., the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw, taken from it;
And Rabbi Yosei deems him exempt from giving those gifts.
What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, whose opinion is the ruling cited first in the mishna?
messages.quote: he is obligated to have the gifts of the priesthood

notes.he: דקתני סתמא דמתני' חייב במתנות:
notes.en: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir: for the unattributed mishna teaches: he is obligated in the gifts.

notes.he: דמחייב במתנות. לר' עקיבא לא צריך למיבעי מ"ט מחייב משום דכיון דמצריך ליה רעייה ומסתאב ודאי דינו שיהא חייב במתנות הואיל ואסתאב ליה אלא לר' מאיר דלא מצריך ליה ליסתאב אמאי מחייב במתנות הא אכתי יש לו דין בכור עליו:
notes.en: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, who obligates in the gifts? [A printed gloss here: “Our master’s words are not understood, for apparently the unattributed mishna, which is Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yosei both speak within the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Tarfon, and according to all, the second grazes until it becomes blemished. This needs study.”] According to Rabbi Akiva there is no need to ask why he obligates, for since he requires it to graze and become blemished, certainly its law is that it is obligated in the gifts once it has become blemished. But according to Rabbi Meir, who does not require it to become blemished, why does he obligate it in the gifts? It still has the law of a firstborn upon it!

notes.he: ואית ספרים דכתיב בהו מ"ט דר' עקיבא ומתרצי נמי לטעמיה הואיל ובא עליו כהן כו':
notes.en: And there are books in which it is written, “What is the reasoning of Rabbi Akiva?”, and they answer in the same way according to his reasoning: since the priest comes upon him, etc.

messages.text: The owner is obligated since the priest comes upon him from two sides, i.e., by force of two complementary claims, as the priest says to him: If the second lamb is in fact the firstborn, it is mine in its entirety, and if it is not the firstborn, at least give me the priestly gifts from it.

notes.he: והאי דשקיל אנא הוי חולין ומהדרנא לך ניהלך ושקילנא מתנות מיניה:
notes.en: If it is a firstborn, all of it is mine: and the one that I took would be non-sacred, and I would return it to you and take the gifts from it.

notes.dh: אמר ר' יוחנן הואיל וכהן בא עליו מב' צדדין כו'
notes.he: ומשום הכי אפי' לא נסתאב חייב במתנות:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Since the priest comes upon him from two sides, etc. And therefore, even if it has not become blemished, he is obligated in the gifts.

messages.text: And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Yosei, who deems the owner exempt from giving the priestly gifts from the second animal?
messages.quote: deems him exempt from giving those gifts

messages.text: In this particular case, the Sages rendered one who did not acquire the animal like one who acquired the animal. And therefore, even though the second lamb of the Israelite did not actually enter the priest’s possession, it is considered as though it entered the priest’s possession and he then sold it to the Israelite in its blemished state, in exchange for the lamb he received. The owner can then claim that perhaps it is the firstborn, and he already fulfilled his obligation of giving it to the priest.

notes.he: והדר שקליה לאידך חילופיה ובכור שמכרו כהן לישראל פטור מן המתנות דאיתקש לצבי ואיל בפרקא קמא (לעיל בכורות דף יב.):
notes.en: And he sold it to the Israelite in its blemish: and then took the other one as its replacement. And a firstborn that a priest sold to an Israelite is exempt from the gifts, since it is compared to the gazelle and the deer, in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 12a).

notes.he: אע"פ שלא זכה כהן בהאיך דהא לא מטא לידיה מעולם עשאוהו כאילו זכה בו הואיל ומעיקרא הוה שייכא ביה יד כהן דשמא דידיה נינהו שויוה רבנן כמאן דמטא לידיה לשום בכורה:
notes.en: They rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires: even though the priest did not acquire that one, since it never reached his hands, they treated it as though he had acquired it. Since from the outset the priest had a hand in it, for perhaps it is his, the Rabbis treated it as though it had reached his hands as a firstborn.

notes.he: הא דאמר בסוף כל הגט (גיטין דף ל.) גבי מלוה מעות את הכהן ואת הלוי להיות מפריש עליהם מחלקם הא מני ר"י דאמר עשו את שאינו זוכה כזוכה ארבי יוסי דהכא קאי דכולה חד טעמא הוא דהתם נמי חליפיו ביד כהן שהרי נתן לו המעות ולא קאי אדרבי יוסי בפ' שנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף יב.) גבי השוכר את הפועל ילקט בנו אחריו דמפרש התם טעמא דר' יוסי משום דעשו שאינו זוכה כזוכה דהתם טעמא אחרינא משום תקנת עניים כדמפר' התם עניים גופייהו ניחא להו וכו' והשתא למאי דפריך לא קשה מידי בהא דפסיק שמואל כר' יוסי בההיא דשנים אוחזין ובגיטין לא בעי לאוקמי מתני' דהתם כר' יוסי אלא אמרי' לא מוקמינן לה כיחידאה שמא דלא סבר לה כר' יוסי בגיטין:
notes.en: They rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires: That which is said at the end of Kol HaGet (Gittin 30a), about one who lends money to a priest or a Levite so as to separate [their gifts] for them from their share, “Whose view is this? Rabbi Yosei, who said they rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires,” refers to the Rabbi Yosei here, since it is all one reasoning: there too his replacement is in the priest’s hand, since he gave him the money. And it does not refer to the Rabbi Yosei of chapter Shnayim Oḥazin (Bava Metzia 12a), about one who hires a laborer, [that] his son may gather [gleanings] after him, where Rabbi Yosei’s reasoning is explained as being that they rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires. For there it is a different reason, an ordinance for the poor, as is explained there: the poor themselves are content with it, etc. And now, according to what [the Gemara there] asks, there is no difficulty in the fact that Shmuel rules like Rabbi Yosei in that case of Shnayim Oḥazin, while in Gittin [the Gemara] does not want to establish the mishna there according to Rabbi Yosei but says, “We do not establish it according to an individual opinion”: for perhaps [Shmuel] does not hold like the Rabbi Yosei of Gittin.

notes.he: עשו את שאינו זוכה בו כהן שהוא ביד ישראל שפטור מן המתנות כזוכה באותו שהוא ביד כהן שפטור ואע"ג דלא זכה ביה באידך שויוה רבנן כמאן דזכה ביה וחשוב כמו שמכרו לישראל בכור במומו בשביל זה שזכה בו כהן לעצמו נמצא שחליפיו דאותו של ישראל הוא ביד כהן ומכר לו הכל הגוף והמתנות הילכך פוטר ר' יוסי:
notes.en: They rendered the one the priest does not acquire, which is in the Israelite’s hand, exempt from the gifts, like the one he does acquire, which is in the priest’s hand and is exempt. Even though he did not acquire that other one, the Rabbis treated it as though he had, and it is regarded as though he sold the Israelite a blemished firstborn in exchange for this one that the priest acquired for himself. It turns out that the replacement for the Israelite’s animal is in the priest’s hand, and he sold him everything, the body and the gifts. Therefore Rabbi Yosei exempts.

messages.text: § Everyone concedes in the case of an animal with uncertain firstborn status, the replacement for which is not in the possession of the priest, that it is obligated to have gifts of the priesthood taken from it. In other words, in a case where the priest receives neither offspring, e.g., when a male and female are born together, all agree that the owner must give the gifts to the priest.

notes.dh: בספק בכור שאין חליפין ביד כהן
notes.he: שלא נטל כלום תחתיו כגון דקתני מתני' זכר ונקבה אין כאן לכהן כלום והאי זכר ספק בכור הוא שמא יצאה נקבה תחלה וירעה ויאכל במומו לבעלים:
notes.en: In an uncertain firstborn whose replacement is not in the hand of the priest: who took nothing in its place, as when the mishna teaches: a male and a female, the priest has nothing here. That male is an uncertain firstborn, since perhaps the female came out first; it grazes, and is eaten in its blemish by the owners.

notes.he: דהכא ליכא למימר עשאוהו כמי שמכרו כהן לישראל דהא לא בא בחליפין ליד כהן כלום:
notes.en: That it is obligated in the gifts: for here one cannot say they treated it as if the priest had sold it to the Israelite, since nothing came into the priest’s hand as a replacement.

notes.dh: הכל מודים בספק בכור שאין חליפיו ביד כהן
notes.he: כגון ספק זכר ונקבה דאין כאן לכהן כלום אותו ודאי חייב במתנות:
notes.en: Everyone concedes in an uncertain firstborn whose replacement is not in the hand of the priest: as in the uncertain case of a male and a female, where the priest has nothing here; that one is certainly obligated in the gifts.

messages.text: When Rabbi Elazar said that everyone concedes, to whom was he referring? Was he referring to Rabbi Yosei? That seems obvious. After all, Rabbi Yosei deemed the owner exempt from giving the gifts only there, where the replacement is in the possession of the priest, as the Sages rendered one who did not acquire the animal like one who acquired the animal.

But if the replacement is not in the possession of the priest, evidently Rabbi Yosei does not rule that one is exempt, as his reasoning does not apply. Why, then, is the statement of Rabbi Elazar necessary?

Rabbi Elazar’s statement is in fact necessary, lest you say that the reason Rabbi Yosei deems him exempt from giving the gifts is that he holds that if you deem him obligated in the gifts, he will assume that the animal is completely non-sacred and come to use it for shearing and labor.

notes.he: לספק בכור במתנות אתי למימר חולין גמור הוא ואתי למישרי בגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: If you deem him obligated: [if you deem] an uncertain firstborn obligated in the gifts, he will come to say it is entirely non-sacred, and will come to permit shearing and labor.

notes.he: לאו משום חליפין אלא משום דאי מחייבת ליה במתנות סבר חולין הוא ואתי לידי גיזה. הילכך דאע"ג דאין חליפין ליפטר:
notes.en: Lest you say Rabbi Yosei’s reason is not because of the replacement, but because if you obligate him in the gifts he will think it is non-sacred and come to shear it; therefore, even though there is no replacement, he should be exempt.

messages.text: Consequently, even though there is no replacement in the hands of the priest, the Sages ruled that one is exempt from giving the gifts, in order to ensure that he does not violate the prohibition against shearing the animal or using it for labor. Rabbi Elazar therefore teaches us that this is not the halakha, as Rabbi Yosei agrees that one is obligated to give the priestly gifts in such circumstances.

notes.he: ר' אלעזר דמשום חליפין הוא והיכא דאין חליפין חייב:
notes.en: It teaches us: Rabbi Elazar [teaches] that it is because of the replacement, and where there is no replacement he is obligated.

messages.text: And how can you say this? But doesn’t the latter clause of the mishna (18b) teach: As Rabbi Yosei says:

notes.he: דטעמא דרבי יוסי משום גיזה ועבודה הוא:
notes.en: And how can you say: that Rabbi Yosei’s reason is because of shearing and labor?

notes.he: דנסיק אדעתין דר' יוסי משום דאי מחייבת ליה אמר:
notes.en: And how can you say this: that it should enter our minds that Rabbi Yosei’s reason is that if you obligate him, he will say [it is non-sacred]?

messages.text: With regard to any animal whose replacements are in the possession of the priest, its owner is exempt from the mitzva of giving the priestly gifts,
And Rabbi Meir deems him obligated to give the gifts.

Evidently, in a case where the replacement is in the possession of the priest, yes, Rabbi Yosei rules that the owner is exempt from giving the gifts, but if the replacement is not in the possession of the priest, he is not exempt.

notes.he: בפירוש ר' יוסי אמר כל שחליפיו כו'. אלמא דטעמיה משום חליפין:
notes.en: But doesn’t the latter clause teach: explicitly, Rabbi Yosei said: Any whose replacements, etc. Evidently his reason is because of the replacement.

messages.text: Even so, Rabbi Elazar’s statement is necessary, lest you say that Rabbi Yosei was not expressing his own opinion but stated his opinion in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Meir, i.e., he said to him:

notes.he: לא בעי חליפין אלא לדבריו דר' מאיר קאמר וכו' להכי איצטריך ר' אלעזר למימר דחייב:
notes.en: Lest you say Rabbi Yosei does not require a replacement, but spoke according to Rabbi Meir’s words, etc. Therefore Rabbi Elazar had to say that he is obligated.

messages.text: @Rabbi Meir In my opinion, the Israelite is exempt from giving the priestly gifts even if the replacement is not in the possession of the priest, as, if you deem him obligated in the gifts, he might think that the animal is completely non-sacred and come to use it for shearing and labor. But even according to your reasoning, at least concede to me in a case where the replacement is in the possession of the priest, that the Sages rendered one who did not acquire the animal like one who acquired the animal.
@Rabbi Yosei No, I do not concede in that case.
Accordingly, Rabbi Elazar is teaching that Rabbi Yosei does, in fact, maintain that the reason for the Israelite’s exemption is that the replacement is in the possession of the priest.
Everyone concedes in the case of an animal whose status as tithe is uncertain that its owner is exempt from the mitzva of the priestly gifts.
messages.lead: And with regard to the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei:

notes.he: כגון שקפץ אחד מן המעושרין לתוכם דאמרינן בפ"ב (לקמן בכורות דף נח:) כולם ירעו עד שיסתאבו ויאכלו במומן לבעלים. ספק מעשר אין כהן בא עליו משני צדדין דאם מעשר הוא אין לכהן חלק בו דמעשר קרב שלמים ונאכל לבעלים:
notes.en: In an uncertain tithe: for example, where one of the tithed animals jumped back among them, of which we say in “chapter 2” [so the printed text; the passage is below, Bekhorot 58b] that all of them graze until they become blemished and are eaten in their blemish by the owners. An uncertain tithe: the priest does not come upon him from two sides, since if it is tithe the priest has no share in it, as tithe is sacrificed as a peace offering and eaten by the owners.

notes.he: כגון קרא לתשיעי עשירי ולעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשין העשירי מעשר והתשיעי קרב במומו ואחד עשר קרב שלמים והיינו ספק מעשר שפטור מן המתנות דאין יכול לבוא עליו משני צדדין וכ"ש מעשר ודאי דפטורה דהוי קדשים קלים וישראל אכיל ליה כוליה חוץ מאימורין:
notes.en: In an uncertain tithe: for example, where he called the ninth “tenth,” the tenth “ninth,” and the eleventh “tenth”: all three are consecrated; the tenth is tithe, the ninth is [eaten] in its blemish [the printed text reads “sacrificed in its blemish”], and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering. That is an uncertain tithe, which is exempt from the gifts, since [the priest] cannot come upon him from two sides. All the more so a certain tithe is exempt, since it is an offering of lesser sanctity and the Israelite eats all of it except the portions burned on the altar.

messages.text: When Rav Pappa says that everyone concedes, to whom is he referring? Is he referring to Rabbi Meir? That would seem obvious. After all, Rabbi Meir deemed one obligated to give the gifts only there, in the case of an animal whose status as firstborn is uncertain, since the priest comes upon the Israelite from two sides.
But with regard to an animal whose status as tithe is uncertain Rabbi Meir does not rule that one is obligated, as that reasoning does not apply. Why, then, is Rav Pappa’s statement necessary?

notes.he: אלמא דאין מחייב ר' מאיר אלא מבכור דבא משני צדדין אבל במעשר לא מחייב ולא איצטריך דרב פפא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Meir obligates [only there]. Evidently Rabbi Meir obligates only for a firstborn, where [the priest] comes from two sides, but for tithe he does not obligate, and Rav Pappa’s statement is not needed.

messages.text: The statement of Rav Pappa is necessary lest you say that the reason that Rabbi Meir deems him obligated in the gifts is so that the halakhic category of the gifts should not be forgotten; if so, the same would apply even in the case of an animal whose status as tithe is uncertain. Rav Pappa therefore teaches us otherwise.

notes.he: אכתי איצטריך מהו דתימא ר' מאיר כו' קמ"ל רב פפא דפטר לדברי הכל:
notes.en: It is still needed: lest you say Rabbi Meir, etc. Rav Pappa teaches us that it is exempt according to all.

messages.text: And how can you say this? But doesn’t the latter clause teach: As Rabbi Yosei says: With regard to any animal whose replacements are in the possession of a priest, its owner is exempt from the mitzva of giving the priestly gifts, and Rabbi Meir deems him obligated to give the gifts.

notes.he: דטעמא דרבי מאיר משום שלא תשתכח תורת מתנות:
notes.en: And how can you say this: that Rabbi Meir’s reason is so that the category of the gifts should not be forgotten?

messages.text: Evidently, the basis for the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei is not whether an obligation is imposed so that the halakhic category of the priestly gifts should not be forgotten, but whether the Sages rendered one who did not acquire the animal like one who acquired the animal, which means that an animal whose replacement is in the priest’s possession is not subject to the mitzva of the gifts.

notes.he: אי אמרת בשלמא טעמא דרבי מאיר גבי בכור משום דבא עליו משני צדדין היינו דקנסיב ר' יוסי הש"ס דהואיל וחליפיו ביד כהן פטור דאינו יכול לומר אי בכור הוא כולו דידי הוא דהוי כמאן דזבניה לישראל אלא אי אמרת טעמא דר' מאיר משום שלא תשתכח תורת מתנות אמאי נקט רבי יוסי טעמא משום דחליפיו ביד כהן הא לר' מאיר נמי מה"ט לפטר אלא ודאי טעמא לאו משום שלא תשתכח תורת מתנות הוא:
notes.en: Any whose replacements, etc.: Granted, if you say that Rabbi Meir’s reason with regard to a firstborn is that [the priest] comes upon him from two sides, that is why Rabbi Yosei took up the reasoning that since its replacement is in the priest’s hand it is exempt: [the priest] cannot say, “If it is a firstborn, it is all mine,” since it is as though he sold it to the Israelite. But if you say Rabbi Meir’s reason is so that the category of the gifts should not be forgotten, why does Rabbi Yosei give the reason that its replacements are in the priest’s hand? For according to Rabbi Meir too, on this reasoning, it should be exempt! Rather, the reason is certainly not so that the category of the gifts should not be forgotten.

messages.text: Rav Pappa’s statement is necessary lest you say: Rabbi Meir deems one obligated to give the gifts even in the case of an animal whose status as tithe is uncertain, in order that the halakhic category of the gifts should not be forgotten.

And as for the fact that the mishna presents their disagreement with regard to replacement animals, this serves to convey to you the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, who deems one exempt from the mitzva of the gifts even in a case where the priest comes upon the Israelite from two sides. Rav Pappa therefore teaches us that in fact Rabbi Meir exempts one from the mitzva of the priestly gifts in the case of an animal whose tithed status is uncertain.
The priest and the owner divide the remaining lamb.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches: If one of the two born together died,

messages.text: Why should they divide it? Let us see: According to Rabbi Tarfon, who holds that it is presumed that the healthier and better of the two emerged first, as explained earlier, if the fatter and better of the two died it should be assumed that it was the one that belonged to the priest, and this one that is left belongs to the owner.
messages.quote: The priest and the owner divide the remaining lamb

notes.he: האי דמית דהא רבי טרפון אמר כהן בורר לו את היפה:
notes.en: If the fat one died, it is the priest’s: this one that died, since Rabbi Tarfon said the priest chooses the better one.

notes.he: הא אמר איהו דהכהן בורר לו את היפה דההוא דבריא נפק ברישא:
notes.en: And why should they divide? He himself said that the priest chooses the better one, since the healthy one came out first.

notes.he: השתא אי שמן מית והיינו דבריא דכהן הוא כו':
notes.en: Let us see: now, if the fat one died, which is the healthy one, it is the priest’s, etc.

messages.text: And if the leaner of the two died, it should be assumed that the animal of the owner died, and this one that is left belongs to the priest.

In fact, Rabbi Tarfon retracted his previous ruling that the priest takes the better of the two, and instead ruled that the priest and owner divide the value of the offspring in all cases. The mishna was not emended to reflect the updated ruling.

notes.he: מקמייתא דאמר כהן בורר לו את היפה וסבר דלשניהם יש חלק בשניהם:
notes.en: Rabbi Tarfon retracted: from his first ruling, where he said the priest chooses the better one; and he holds that both have a share in both.

notes.he: ממאי דאמר מעיקרא בורר אלא סבר דיחלוקו אפי' שניהם חיים:
notes.en: Rabbi Tarfon retracted: from what he had said at first, that [the priest] chooses; rather he holds that they divide, even when both are alive.

messages.text: The living offspring remains in the possession of the owner, as the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches: In a case where two animals were born together and one of them died,

notes.dh: ר' עקיבא אמר המוציא מחברו עליו הראיה כו'
notes.he: כלומר דברשותא דבעה"ב קאי וכהן בעי איתויי ראיה:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva says: The burden of proof rests upon the claimant, etc. That is, it stands in the homeowner’s possession, and the priest must bring a proof.

messages.text: To what is this matter comparable? It is comparable to two people who each deposited a sheep with a shepherd and one of the two sheep died, and it is unclear to whom it belonged. In that case, the shepherd places the remaining sheep between them and withdraws, leaving them to divide the value of the sheep between them. Likewise, the mishna is discussing a case where the live offspring is not in the possession of either the owner or the priest, and therefore it is divided between them.
messages.lead: Rabbi Ḥiyya stated a parable that clarifies the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon, who says that the priest and the owner divide the remaining lamb:

notes.he: שתי בהמות ומתה האחת ואין ידוע של מי מתה:
notes.en: To two who deposited with a shepherd: two animals, and one of them died, and it is not known whose died.

notes.he: בין שניהם לחלקה ומסתלק דהכא ליכא למימר המוציא מחבירו ומתני' נמי דקאמר רבי טרפון יחלוקו כגון שאותו ספק בכור החי נמסר לרועה ואתי בעל הבית וכהן גבי רועה דליכא מוציא מחבירו דהא לא קאי ברשותא דחד מינייהו:
notes.en: That the shepherd places: [it] between the two of them to divide, and withdraws; for here one cannot say “the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.” And in the mishna too, where Rabbi Tarfon says they divide, it is a case where that living uncertain firstborn was handed over to a shepherd, and the homeowner and the priest come to the shepherd; so there is no claimant taking from his fellow, since it is not in the possession of either of them.

notes.he: לשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה שתי בהמות ומתה אחת מהן ואין יודע הרועה של מי המתה וזהו הדין שמניח החייה בינייהו ומסתלק והוי ממון מוטל בספק וחולקין. כך האחד שהוא חי מנח ביניהן בין כהן לישראל הילכך חולקין:
notes.en: To two who deposited two animals with a shepherd, and one of them died, and the shepherd does not know whose died: the law is that he places the living one between them and withdraws, and it is money lying in doubt, and they divide. So too the one that is alive is placed between them, between the priest and the Israelite; therefore they divide.

messages.text: To what is this matter comparable? It is comparable to one who deposited a sheep with a homeowner, who had sheep of his own, and it is unknown whose sheep died. In that case, the burden of proof rests upon the claimant. Since the remaining sheep is currently in the possession of the homeowner, the one who deposited the animal must prove that the living sheep belongs to him. Likewise, the mishna is discussing a case where the live offspring is in the possession of the owner, and therefore the burden of proof rests upon the priest.
messages.lead: And Rabbi Ḥiyya also stated a parable that clarifies the opinion of Rabbi Akiva:

notes.dh: ומשל דרבי עקיבא לאחד שהפקיד אצל בעל הבית
notes.he: והניחה בעדרו ומתה בהמה אחת בעדרו ואומר שלך מתה והלה אומר אחת מאותן שלך מתה המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה ומתני' נמי דמרע ליה ר' עקיבא לכחו של כהן כשישנן ברשות בעל הבית דהוי כהן מוציא מחבירו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva’s parable, to one who deposited with a homeowner: and he put it in his flock, and one animal in his flock died, and he says: Yours died, and the other says: One of yours died. The burden of proof rests upon the claimant. And in the mishna too, where Rabbi Akiva weakens the priest’s position, it is when they are in the homeowner’s possession, so the priest is a claimant taking from his fellow.

notes.dh: לאחד שהפקיד אצל בעל הבית בהמה אחת
notes.he: וערבה בעדרו ומת אחד מהעדר ואין ידוע אם משל בעל הבית הוא או של מפקיד וזהו הדין המוציא מחברו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: To one who deposited one animal with a homeowner, and it mixed into his flock, and one of the flock died, and it is not known whether it is the homeowner’s or the depositor’s: the law there is that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

messages.text: But if Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva are addressing different circumstances, then with regard to what matter do they disagree? Does Rabbi Akiva disagree with the conclusion in the parable mentioned with regard to Rabbi Tarfon’s opinion, of two people who each deposited a sheep with a shepherd, that the shepherd places the remaining sheep between them and withdraws?

notes.he: הואיל ולאו בחד גונא קמיתרצא מתני':
notes.en: Rather, about what do they disagree: since the mishna is not explained as one and the same case.

notes.dh: ר' עקיבא פליג בשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה
notes.he: בתמיה. הא ודאי ליכא למימר המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: Does Rabbi Akiva disagree about two who deposited with a shepherd: said in astonishment. There, certainly, one cannot say “the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.”

notes.he: הואיל ור' חייא אמר דנראין דברי זה ודברי זה ומביא ראיה לזה ולזה אלא במאי פליגי אמאי לא מודו אהדדי והלא שניהן שוים שהפקידו אצל רועה דהכי דינן ושוין נמי באחד שהפקיד אצל בעל הבית. (לאו) ר' עקיבא פליג בשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה. אע"ג דאיכא למימר שרועה מניח ביניהם ומסתלק אפי' הכי קאמר ר' עקיבא שהמוציא מחברו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: Rather, about what do they disagree? Since Rabbi Ḥiyya says that the words of this one and the words of that one appear [right], and brings a proof for each, about what do they disagree? Why do they not concede to each other? Are not both agreed about two who deposited with a shepherd, that such is the law, and agreed too about one who deposited with a homeowner? Does Rabbi Akiva disagree about two who deposited with a shepherd? [That is,] even though one can say that the shepherd places it between them and withdraws, does Rabbi Akiva nevertheless say that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant?

messages.text: And similarly, does Rabbi Tarfon disagree with the conclusion in the case of one who deposited a sheep with a homeowner that the homeowner keeps the remaining sheep? Certainly not.

notes.he: כלומר דלא פליגי אלא הכל מודים בשנים ובאחד כו':
notes.en: And does Rabbi Tarfon disagree about one who deposited? That is, they do not disagree; rather, everyone concedes about two and about one, etc.

messages.alt: and some say it was Rav Pappa
messages.text: Everyone concedes in the case of two who deposited sheep with a shepherd that the shepherd places it between them and withdraws, and everyone concedes in the case of one who deposited a sheep with a homeowner that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

notes.dh: הכל מודים בשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה כו'
notes.he: בפרק המפקיד (ב"מ דף לז:) פריך דרבא אדרבא אהא דאמר רבא דבשתי כריכות הוה ליה למידק כו':
notes.en: Everyone concedes about two who deposited with a shepherd, etc.: In chapter HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 37b), [the Gemara] raises a contradiction between this statement of Rava and another statement of Rava, about what Rava said, that in the case of two bundles he should have been careful, etc.

notes.he: אין זה כי ההוא דגזל אחד מחמשה בני אדם דאמרי' מניח גזילה ביניהם ומסתלק ופריך בפ' המפקיד (שם.) ושקלי ליה כולהו ואזלי והאמר ר' אבא בר זבדא ספק הנוח לכתחלה לא יטול ואם נטל לא יחזיר ומפרש דמניח דקאמר גבי גזל היינו שיניח בידו או ביד בית דין עד שיתברר של מי הוא אבל הכא לא חיישינן אי שקלי לה כולהו ואזלי דמיירי כשהפקידו לו שלא מדעתו ואינו מוטל עליו לשמור ולא הוי בספק הינוח ואי מסתלק דהכא בעי למימר שיחלוקו ביניהם הוי ממש כמו דרבי טרפון ואם רוצה לומר מסתלק וכל דאלים גבר צריך לומר דהא דמדמי להא דר' טרפון לשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה הכי קאמר דכיון דהתם כל דאלים גבר ולא אמרינן ביה המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה סברא הוא לתקן כמו כן גבי כהן (שיחלוקו):
notes.en: That the shepherd places it between them and withdraws: This is not like the case of one who robbed one of five people, where we say he places the stolen item between them and withdraws, and [the Gemara] asks in chapter HaMafkid (ibid.): But then they will all take it and go! And didn’t Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say: An uncertain item that is left aside, one should not take ab initio, and if one took it, one need not return it? And it explains that “places,” said about the robber, means that he leaves it in his own hand or in the hand of the court until it is clarified whose it is. But here we are not concerned if they all take it and go, since it is a case where they deposited with him without his consent, and he is not obligated to guard it, and it is not an item left aside in uncertainty. And if “withdraws” here means that they divide between them, it is exactly like Rabbi Tarfon’s ruling. And if it means “withdraws, and whoever is stronger prevails,” one must say that when [the Gemara] compares Rabbi Tarfon’s case to two who deposited with a shepherd, it means this: since there, whoever is stronger prevails and we do not say “the burden of proof rests upon the claimant,” it is reasonable to institute likewise with the priest (that they divide).

notes.dh: הכל מודים בשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה
notes.he: היינו אם מסר בעה"ב בהמתו שלא ביכרה לרועה דיש עליה נמי רשות כהן וילדה ב' זכרים ברשות הרועה ודאי יש דין שיחלוקו. ובאחד שהפקיד אצל בעה"ב כגון שברשות בעה"ב והבהמה מסרה בעה"ב לרועה כהן:
notes.en: Everyone concedes about two who deposited with a shepherd: that is, if the homeowner handed his animal that had not given birth to a shepherd, so that the priest too has a claim on it, and it gave birth to two males in the shepherd’s possession, certainly the law is that they divide. And about one who deposited with a homeowner: for example, where it is in the homeowner’s possession, and the homeowner handed the animal to a priest who is a shepherd.

messages.text: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Tarfon disagree only where the offspring were born in the courtyard of the homeowner, and the shepherd is a priest to whom the homeowner usually gives his firstborn animals.

notes.he: כגון שהבכור חי עומד בחצר בעל הבית וכהן רועה כל בהמותיו של בעל הבית:
notes.en: They disagree only: for example, where the living firstborn stands in the homeowner’s courtyard, and a priest tends all of the homeowner’s animals.

messages.text: Rabbi Tarfon holds: The homeowner transfers to the priest a portion of his courtyard so that the priest should acquire the firstborn offspring located there, because it is suitable for him that the mitzva of giving the firstborn to a priest should be performed. Therefore, the priest is considered to hold partial jurisdiction of the courtyard.

notes.he: בעל הבית לכהן מקום בחצירו כדי שיזכה כהן בבכורות כשיוולדו מיד דתיקני ליה חצירו:
notes.en: He transfers to him: the homeowner [transfers] to the priest a place in his courtyard, so that the priest acquires the firstborn animals as soon as they are born, his courtyard acquiring them for him.

notes.dh: דניחא ליה לאינש דתתעביד מצוה בממוניה
notes.he: שיגדלו בכורותיו של כהן בחצירו והוה ליה חצר של שניהם והוי האי חצר כי רועה וכאילו שנים הפקידו אצלו הילכך חולקין דברשות שניהם עומד:
notes.en: For a person is content that a mitzva be performed with his property: that the priest’s firstborn animals be raised in his courtyard. So it becomes the courtyard of both of them, and this courtyard is like the shepherd, as though two had deposited with him. Therefore they divide, since it stands in the possession of both.

notes.dh: אקנויי קא מקני ליה מקום בחצרו
notes.he: ואפי' בלא קנין קא קני דגמר ומשעבד נפשיה אי נמי כמה פעמים הרועה פותח ונועל כדאמר תיזיל איהי ותחוד ותפתח וברשות בעל הבית קא מחזיק:
notes.en: He transfers to him a place in his courtyard: And even without a formal act of acquisition [the priest] acquires, since [the homeowner] resolves to do so and binds himself. Alternatively, the shepherd often opens and locks, as it is said, “Let her go and lock and open,” and so he takes possession in the homeowner’s property.

notes.dh: ר' טרפון סבר אקנויי אקני ליה
notes.he: בעה"ב לרועה כהן מקום בחצרו שיהיה בכורו שם דניחא ליה לבעה"ב דתיתעביד מצוה בחצרו שיגדל בכורו של כהן שם והוה ליה כשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה ב' הן הכהן ובעה"ב והחצר היא הרועה שיש לשניהם רשות בה:
notes.en: Rabbi Tarfon holds: he transfers to him. The homeowner [transfers] to the priestly shepherd a place in his courtyard where his firstborn will be, for the homeowner is content that a mitzva be done in his courtyard, that the priest’s firstborn be raised there. So it is like two who deposited with a shepherd: the two are the priest and the homeowner, and the courtyard is the shepherd, since both have rights in it.

messages.text: And consequently, this is comparable to two people who each deposited a sheep with a shepherd and one of the two sheep died, where the shepherd places the remaining sheep between them and withdraws, leaving them to divide the value of the sheep between themselves.

notes.he: הילכך יחלוקו:
notes.en: That he places the stolen item [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf here speaks of the shepherd placing the animal] between them: therefore they divide.

messages.text: And Rabbi Akiva holds: Since there is a loss to the owner in this case of uncertainty, he does not transfer anything to the priest. And as the courtyard belongs exclusively to the Israelite, this case is comparable to one who deposited a sheep with a homeowner who had sheep of his own, and it is unknown whose sheep died. The halakha in that case is that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

notes.he: היכא דאיכא ספיקא מפסיד בעל הבית אי קיימא חצר ברשות כהן:
notes.en: A loss: where there is an uncertainty, the homeowner loses if the courtyard stands in the priest’s possession.

notes.dh: ור' עקיבא סבר כיון דאית ליה פסידא
notes.he: לבעל הבית דזימנין דמית הבכור ואתי כהן ואמר לא בכור מית אלא חדא בהמה דידך מית ומשום הא חששא לא מקני ליה מקום והוה ליה כהן אצל חצר כאחד שהפקידו אצל בעה"ב והמוציא מחברו ע"ה. להכי נקט שנים שהפקידו אצל רועה ואחד שהפקידו אצל בעה"ב שכן דרך בני אדם ב' מפקידין בהמתן אצל רועה ואחד דרכו להפקיד אצל בעה"ב:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva holds: since there is a loss to the homeowner, for sometimes the firstborn dies, and the priest comes and says: It was not the firstborn that died, but one of your animals. Because of this concern he does not transfer a place to him, and the priest at the courtyard is like one who deposited with a homeowner, and the burden of proof rests upon the claimant. [The Gemara] chose “two who deposited with a shepherd” and “one who deposited with a homeowner” because it is people’s way for two to deposit their animals with a shepherd, and for one to deposit with a homeowner.

messages.text: Mishna
If one’s two ewes had not previously given birth and they gave birth to two males, both of them are given to the priest, as each is its mother’s firstborn.
If one gave birth to a male and the other to a female, the male is given to the priest, as it is its mother’s firstborn.
If they gave birth to two males and a female, one of the males is kept by him and one is given to the priest.

notes.he: שהרי היתה נקבה עמו ואיכא למימר נקבה יצאת תחלה:
notes.en: Mishna. One is his: since there was a female with it, one can say the female came out first.

messages.text: The priest chooses the better of the two.
They assess the value of the lambs between them, and the priest takes the leaner of the two.

notes.he: כהן נוטל כחוש:
notes.en: They assess between them: the priest takes the lean one.

messages.text: And the second lamb must graze until it becomes blemished, at which point the owner may slaughter and eat it.
And when the owner slaughters the animal, he is obligated to have gifts of the priesthood, i.e., the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw, taken from it.
Rabbi Yosei deems him exempt from giving the gifts.
If one of the two born together died:
The priest and the owner divide the value of the remaining lamb.

notes.he: דחזר בו ר' טרפון מקמייתא:
notes.en: They divide: for Rabbi Tarfon retracted from his first ruling.

messages.text: Since there is uncertainty to whom it belongs, it remains in the possession of the owner, as the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.
If they gave birth to two females and a male or to two males and two females, the priest has nothing here, as perhaps both ewes gave birth to females first.

notes.dh: שני זכרים ושתי נקבות אין כאן לכהן כלום
notes.he: דאיכא למימר כל חדא וחדא ילדה זכר ונקבה ויצאת נקבה תחלה:
notes.en: Two males and two females, the priest has nothing here: for one can say that each one bore a male and a female, and the female came out first.

messages.text: If one of his ewes had previously given birth and one had not previously given birth, and they gave birth to two males, one of the males is kept by him and one is given to the priest.
The priest chooses the better of the two.
They assess the value of the lambs between them and the priest takes the leaner of the two.
And the second lamb must graze until it becomes blemished, at which point he may slaughter and eat it.
And when he slaughters the animal he is obligated to have gifts of the priesthood taken from it.

Rabbi Yosei deems him exempt from giving those gifts, as Rabbi Yosei says: With regard to any animal whose replacements are in the possession of a priest, its owner is exempt from the mitzva of giving the priestly gifts.

notes.he: שהכהן נוטל אחת מן הספיקות פטור האחר מן המתנות דעשו את שאינו זוכה כזוכה:
notes.en: Whose replacements are in the hand of the priest: since the priest takes one of the uncertain ones, the other is exempt from the gifts, since they rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires.

messages.text: And Rabbi Meir deems him obligated to give the gifts.
If one of the animals died:
The priest and the owner divide the value of the remaining lamb.
Since there is uncertainty to whom it belongs, it remains in the possession of the owner, as the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

If a male and a female offspring were born together, everyone agrees that the priest has nothing here, as perhaps the one that had already given birth bore the male, and the one that had not given birth bore the female, in which case neither of the animals would have firstborn status.

notes.dh: זכר ונקבה אין כאן לכהן כלום
notes.he: דשמא אותה שלא ביכרה ילדה הנקבה ואותה שכבר ביכרה ילדה זכר:
notes.en: A male and a female, the priest has nothing here: for perhaps the one that had not given birth bore the female, and the one that had already given birth bore the male.

messages.caption: The mishna’s cases of two ewes giving birth together, and what the priest receives in each.

messages.text: Gemara

This mishna and the previous mishna (17a–b) listed three cases in which Rabbi Akiva rules that the priest receives the leaner of two potentially firstborn offspring, whereas Rabbi Tarfon maintains that he receives the better of the two. It was necessary to teach each of these three cases,
messages.quote: two males and a female, one by him and one to the priest

notes.he: רחל שילדה שני זכרים התם קאמר ר"ע כהן נוטל כחוש:
notes.en: Gemara. The first: a ewe that bore two males; there Rabbi Akiva says the priest takes the lean one.

messages.text: as, had the mishna taught only the first case, that of a single ewe that gave birth to two male offspring, one might have thought that Rabbi Akiva stated his opinion only in that case, as the two offspring came from one womb, and there is no reason to assume that the better offspring was born first.

notes.he: רחל נפוק ומספקא מילתא והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: Because two from one: [the two] came out of one ewe, and the matter is uncertain, and the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

messages.text: But in the second case, that of his two ewes which had not previously given birth and which collectively gave birth to two males and a female, where two offspring came from one mother and one offspring came from one other mother, one might say that Rabbi Akiva concedes to the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon, as it can be claimed that the superior animal is this one that came from the mother that gave birth to a single offspring.

notes.he: שילדו שני זכרים ונקבה דתרי נפקו מחדא וחד מחדא:
notes.en: But two ewes: that bore two males and a female, where two came out of one and one from the other.

notes.he: דכהן בורר לו את היפה דלפיכך הוא יפה שיצא יחיד ולא היתה הנקבה עמו וזהו ודאי בכור גמור:
notes.en: Say he concedes to Rabbi Tarfon: that the priest chooses the better one, for it is better precisely because it came out alone and the female was not with it, and this one is certainly a full firstborn.

notes.he: שביח מעולה:
notes.en: And this one that bore a single one is superior: shevi’aḥ means excellent.

notes.he: דהך דילדה חד שביח טפי שהיה בריוח שלא דחקו אחד והוא הבכור ודאי ולימא אפי' לר' עקיבא יטול השמן הכהן:
notes.en: For the one that bore a single offspring is superior: since it had room, as no other one pressed it, and it is the certain firstborn; so one might say that even according to Rabbi Akiva the priest takes the fat one.

messages.text: And had the mishna taught only that second case, one might have thought that Rabbi Akiva stated his opinion only in that case, as both mothers had not previously given birth. But in a case where one had previously given birth and the other one had not previously given birth, and collectively they gave birth to two male offspring, one might say that Rabbi Akiva concedes to the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon…

notes.he: בהא ב' רחילות שלא ביכרו קאמר ר"ע דהכהן נוטל כחוש משום דתרוייהו לא ביכרו ומספקא לן איזו ילדה הכחוש אם זו שילדה זכר ונקבה אם זו שילדה זכר לבדו שצריך ראיה דהא לא בכיר שביח טפי ויטול הכהן הבריא צריכא דבכולהו פליג ר"ע:
notes.en: In this case of two ewes that had not given birth, Rabbi Akiva says the priest takes the lean one, since neither had given birth, and we are uncertain which one bore the lean one, whether the one that bore a male and a female or the one that bore a male alone, so a proof is needed. [A printed gloss: It seems one should read: “But where one had given birth and one had not, the one that had not given birth is superior, and one might say the priest takes the healthy one; it was necessary, etc.”] For the one that had not given birth is superior, and [one might say] the priest takes the healthy one. It was necessary [to teach them all], since in all of them Rabbi Akiva disagrees.

messages.text: Continues on 19a: …since the offspring of the ewe that had not given birth before may be the superior one. So each case had to be taught. Then a new mishna: an animal born by caesarean section and the one that follows it.
